title: Meta Muse Character & Personality: The Soul.md Guide
description: Muse has no custom-instructions box. Its personality lives in a Soul.md file you can edit. The tap path, what to paste, how to test it, how to reset it.
h1: Give Meta Muse a character: the Soul.md guide.
dek: Soul.md, Identity.md and Memory.md: which file does what, and what to paste.
lede: Muse lets you customize its communication style through chat or by editing Soul.md. Both are documented controls; we have not established that one works better. Save your original instructions, make a small change, inspect the saved text and test it on representative tasks.
answer: Open Assistant icon → Identity → Soul to edit Soul.md, or request the change in chat and inspect the saved file. Append one clearly labeled preference block and keep a backup. To remove it, restore the edited lines. A whole-account reset also deletes history, files and tasks.

sections.html: For ready-to-copy starting points, use the Muse Soul.md templates: four with Markdown downloads (concise assistant, thinking partner, writing editor, task coordinator) and sixteen by role, from founder to inbox triage. Each is a block to paste at the end of Soul.md and edit.

1. In the Muse app, tap the Assistant icon (your Muse's avatar), then Identity, then Soul.
  2. Add a section at the end of the file and paste the block below, or any tuning from the library.
  3. Inspect the saved text, then try the same representative tasks before and after the edit in fresh conversations. A greeting alone cannot establish compliance.
# How to talk to me - Lead with the answer or the recommendation. Reasoning comes after. - State material uncertainty and missing information plainly. - Give one recommendation, not a menu, unless I ask for options. - Push back when I'm wrong, and say why. - No openers like "Great question", no recap of what I just said, no closing offers.

Add to the file. Don't replace it. Soul.md also holds the core truths and boundaries Muse works from, and you want those left alone. A heading of your own, like the one in the block above, keeps your rules easy to find and easy to delete.

That path is from Meta's help article on managing your Muse data, which says you can edit and delete information in Soul.md directly. Its instructions say tap, so they describe the mobile app. Check the controls in your own client if the menus differ.

This guide covers Meta Muse’s documented files and customization controls. Do not assume they apply to Meta AI in other apps. The supplied questionnaire report names Muse Spark 1.3; it does not verify the model serving every current product session. See the Muse explainer for current source-linked product information and plans.

FileWhat Meta says it holdsWherePut this in it
Soul.mdWho your Muse is: core truths, boundaries, personalityAssistant icon, then Identity, then SoulCommunication rules. How it should talk to you, report to you, disagree with you.
Identity.mdIts name, creature, vibe and taglineAssistant icon, then Identity, then EditIdentity details. Meta does not establish that these have no effect on responses.
Memory.mdFacts about you it has savedAssistant icon, then Identity, then MemorySaved facts such as your name, time zone and work.

Use Soul.md for explicit communication preferences, and inspect Identity.md when changing the name or vibe. This is Meta’s documented division of the files, not proof that the fields cannot interact. See Meta’s data and file controls for the paths available in its documentation.

sections.h2: Option one: tell it in chat.
sections.html:
This is the route Meta documents first. Ask, and Muse saves the change so it carries across conversations. Meta's own list of what you can change this way: its name, its personality and tone, its communication style, what it remembers about you, and its avatar and tagline. Meta's examples of a nudge are 'too long' and 'be more casual'.

A concrete rule is easier to inspect than a vague description. Ask Muse to show the proposed change, then check the file:

Add these rules to your Soul file, under a heading called "How to talk to me". Don't change anything else in the file. Then show me what you added. [paste a character block from below]

Then open Soul.md and read it. It is your file.

sections.h2: Option two: paste a tuning into Soul.md.
sections.html:
Editing the file lets you inspect the exact text.

  1. Pick a tuning from the library and copy the rules. You want the Markdown body: everything below the settings header, which is the block between the two --- lines at the top of the file.
  2. Tap the Assistant icon, then Identity, then Soul.
  3. Paste at the end of the file, under its own heading.
  4. Save, and test in chat.

Meta does not publish a length limit for Soul.md. The Markdown rule bodies run from about 1,200 to 2,900 characters, excluding the metadata header, check the editor for any current size limit before saving.

Which tuning? Match it to you, not to Muse. If you know your MBTI, Enneagram, DISC, Big Five or attachment type, install that file. If you don't, the free MBTI test takes about five minutes and links to the matching file when you finish.

sections.h2: Write rules for reports and approval requests.
sections.html:
For an assistant that can act through connected services, specify how you want proposed actions and verified results presented. For example: “When approval is needed, state the action, known cost and consequence together. Do not claim completion without evidence.”

A communication preference does not set tool permissions. Meta describes separate approval checks whose requirements depend on the action, connector and permissions you select. Review those settings independently. Test report formatting on a draft task before relying on it for consequential work.

sections.h2: Does it stick? Test and undo the change.
sections.html:
Inspect the saved file and repeat fixed tasks in new conversations. The Muse persistence kit provides probes and a blank log; it contains no measured persistence results.

Restore your backed-up text to undo only your edit. Meta also documents asking Muse to return to its default personality; inspect what changed afterward. A whole-account reset permanently deletes history, files and active tasks and is unnecessary for removing one instruction block.

A personality file says a lot about you. Two facts from Meta's help pages:

  • The setting that lets Meta use your interactions to train its models is on when you first use Muse. It is under Settings, Data controls, Help improve our AI models. Meta says it removes certain identifiers and that you can switch it off at any time.
  • If you import memory from another assistant (Settings, Data Controls, Import memory), everything in that export becomes material Muse can use.

The report reached us on September 24, 2026. Each test was answered 100 times, sequentially, inside one session per test, as Muse's own assistant identity. No raw answer vectors or harness were supplied, so we could not re-score anything; the figures below are transcribed. They sit on the research hub marked reported, next to the four models that answered in fresh sessions with every answer published.

TestMuse Spark 1.3, 100 runs, reported
MBTIISTJ 80 · ISFJ 12 · INTJ 8. Every reported label contains I and J; 92 contain S. These letter counts include tied-axis assignments. Twenty-one runs had a tied axis, resolved by the original reporting rule.
EnneagramHelper (Type 2) labels in 78 runs, Reformer (1) in 15; the report describes 2w1 as its usual wing. Twenty runs reportedly tied at the top; the supplied Type 2 and Type 1 counts do not account for the other seven labels. Type means of 20: 2 = 16.8, 1 = 14.7, 7 = 13.9, 8 = 13.9, 5 = 12.9, 6 = 12.8, 3 = 12.1, 9 = 12.0, 4 = 7.2.
DISCSteadiness first in 55 runs, Conscientiousness first in 45. Means of 20: D 5.1, I 10.9, S 15.2, C 15.6.
AttachmentSecure in all 100. Anxiety 2.04, avoidance 2.52 on 1 to 7 scales where 4 is the cutoff.
Big Five (of 50)Openness 39.5 · Conscientiousness 41.2 · Extraversion 33.8 · Agreeableness 44.6 · Neuroticism 15.6

The report does not establish a default personality, task behavior or a benefit from tuning. Read the full Muse evidence note for ties and missing data.

sections.h2: What the research can and cannot establish.
sections.html:
These are exploratory reports of model-generated self-descriptions, not a validated measure of AI personality or evidence that personality matching improves outcomes. The MBTI total includes repeated scoring of a single answer vector for GLM, Grok, and MiniMax; it does not represent 600 independent model responses. Protocols differed across models. See the methodology and limitations.

Use a type or trait as a starting hypothesis for your preferences. The reports do not establish that one framework produces better instructions, that every model shares a default personality, or that those historical results apply to later model versions. Compare outputs on your own tasks and retain only rules that help.

faq.a: Muse Spark 1.3 was reported as ISTJ in 80 of 100 runs, with ISFJ in 12 and INTJ in eight. The report also lists Type 2 Enneagram labels in 78 runs and Secure attachment labels in 100. These aggregate figures were supplied without raw answer vectors, so AgentTune has not independently re-scored them.

Not under that name. Meta's help center has no custom-instructions box for Muse. The equivalent is Soul.md, a file that holds who your Muse is, including its personality. Tap the Assistant icon, then Identity, then Soul to open and edit it. You can also ask Muse in chat to change its tone or style.

faq.q: Where is Soul.md in the Muse app?
faq.a: Tap the Assistant icon, which is your Muse's avatar, then Identity, then Soul. Meta's help article on managing Muse data says you can edit and delete information in the Soul.md file directly. Meta documents this path for the mobile app only.

faq.q: What is the difference between Soul.md, Identity.md and Memory.md?
faq.a: Soul.md holds who your Muse is: core truths, boundaries and personality. Identity.md holds its name, creature, vibe and tagline. Memory.md holds facts about you, such as your name, time zone and interests. Communication rules belong in Soul.md.

faq.q: How do I reset Muse's personality?
faq.a: Say "Go back to your default personality." Meta documents that phrase, and Muse confirms what it reset. To remove one rule, delete it from Soul.md. A full reset under Settings, Data Controls, Reset wipes chat history, files and active tasks as well.

faq.q: Can I change Muse's name and avatar?
faq.a: Yes. Ask in chat, or tap the Assistant icon, then Identity, then Edit to change Identity.md, which holds the name, creature, vibe and tagline. This changes what Muse is called, not how it communicates.

faq.q: Do the changes work in WhatsApp?
faq.a: Meta says customizations are saved and carry over between conversations, and you can message the same Muse from WhatsApp. Meta does not document whether the Identity editor is available inside WhatsApp, so make file edits in the Muse app, or ask for the change in chat.

faq.q: Is Muse the same as Meta AI?
faq.a: No. Meta AI is the assistant inside Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger. Muse is a separate personal agent with its own app, launched September 8, 2026. It runs on a dedicated cloud computer and takes actions for you. It is powered by the Muse Spark model.

faq.q: Does Meta train on what I write in Soul.md?
faq.a: Meta's help page says the setting that allows your interactions with Muse to be used for training is on when you first use Muse. You can turn it off under Settings, Data controls, Help improve our AI models. Meta does not say specifically how the identity files are treated.

There is a free tier with a usage limit that refreshes. Paid plans are Power at $20 a month with 500M Muse tokens a week, and Maximum at $100 a month with 3B a week. At launch Muse is available in the United States to adults.
